summary: The enterprise AI model API landscape in 2026 is crowded and contested, with no single winner — only a best fit for each organization's existing cloud footprint, governance needs, and model preferences. The dominant pattern is the 'aggregator' model: cloud platforms that expose multiple foundation models (Claude, GPT, Llama, Gemini, Mistral, and more) behind a single secure, managed API so corporate data never leaves the governed cloud perimeter. The big three (AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI/Foundry, Google Vertex AI) lead on adoption, while Snowflake Cortex and IBM watsonx are gaining momentum by embedding AI inside governed data estates.
why_enterprises_use_aggregators: Data residency and security — inference runs inside the company's own cloud VPC/perimeter, so prompts and proprietary data never leave the governed environment or get used for third-party model training.
Compliance and governance — aggregators ship with audit logs, access controls, regional data pinning, and certifications (SOC 2, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FedRAMP) that raw vendor APIs often lack.
Single billing and consolidated procurement — one contract and one bill through an existing cloud vendor instead of negotiating separately with OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, Mistral, etc.
Leverage existing cloud commitments — enterprises can spend down AWS/Azure/GCP committed-spend agreements and reuse existing IAM, networking, and security tooling.
Model choice and portability — access many models behind one consistent API, avoiding lock-in to a single model provider and enabling easy swap/benchmarking in a proof of concept.

platforms.name: Azure OpenAI Service / Azure AI Foundry
available_models: select open models via Foundry Model Catalog
platforms.pricing: Pay-as-you-go per 1K/1M tokens, plus Provisioned Throughput Units (PTUs) for reserved capacity; billed through Azure contracts.
key_features: Content filtering and responsible AI controls
Native Azure AI Search RAG integration
platforms.best_for: Microsoft-first enterprises needing frontier GPT models inside the Azure governance and compliance boundary.

platforms.name: AWS Bedrock
platforms.pricing: On-demand per-token pricing plus Provisioned Throughput for reserved capacity; consolidated on the AWS bill.
platforms.best_for: AWS-centric enterprises wanting the widest multi-provider model choice behind one API.

platforms.name: Google Vertex AI Model Garden
platforms.pricing: Pay-as-you-go per token/character; GSUs (Generative AI Scale Units) for provisioned throughput — e.g. 25 GSUs of Gemini 2.5 Flash yields roughly 67,250 tokens/second sustained.
platforms.best_for: Google Cloud shops and teams wanting Gemini plus a huge Model Garden and strong data/analytics integration.

platforms.name: Snowflake Cortex AI
platforms.pricing: Consumption-based, billed in Snowflake credits and reported under product revenue ($996.8M Q1 FY2026, up 26% YoY).
key_features: AI runs inside the governed Snowflake data perimeter — no data movement
platforms.best_for: Enterprises wanting AI, search, and agents directly on top of governed Snowflake data without exporting it.

platforms.name: IBM watsonx
platforms.pricing: Consumption-based tokens plus subscription/enterprise licensing; deployable on-prem, hybrid, or IBM Cloud.
platforms.best_for: Regulated enterprises with existing IBM relationships needing strong governance, hybrid deployment, and AI risk management.

platforms.name: Databricks Mosaic AI
platforms.pricing: Consumption-based (DBUs) for model serving, training, and inference; billed through Databricks/underlying cloud.
key_features: Model serving and fine-tuning on governed Lakehouse data
platforms.best_for: Data engineering and ML teams building custom AI directly on top of a governed Lakehouse.

platforms.name: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) Generative AI
platforms.pricing: Pay-as-you-go per token plus dedicated AI cluster (reserved capacity) pricing on OCI.
platforms.best_for: Oracle-centric enterprises and public-sector/sovereign deployments needing AI near Oracle applications and data.

platforms.name: Cloudflare Workers AI
available_models: embedding and image models served at the edge
AI Gateway proxying to external providers
platforms.pricing: Usage-based 'Neurons' pricing with a free allowance; serverless per-request/edge pricing.
key_features: AI Gateway for caching, rate limiting, logging, and model routing
platforms.best_for: Developers and enterprises needing low-latency edge inference and a lightweight gateway in front of many model providers.
